summary: Leon Hurvitz was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He served as a professor at the University of Washington (circa 1962–1971) and held posts at the University of British Columbia (circa 1971–1992).

A linguist, Leonard Bloomfield studied at Harvard, Wisconsin-Madison, Chicago under Francis Asbury Wood, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held posts at Illinois (1910–1921), Ohio State (1921–1927), Chicago (1927–1940), and Yale (1940–1949).
Leonard Blussé is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Leiden University from circa 1965 to 1972 and later held a post there from 1998 to 2011.

Leonard C. D. C. Priestley worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under F. E. L. Priestley and doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder. He held a post at the University of Toronto, attested in 1991.

Working in religious studies and philosophy, Leonard Swidler studied at institutions including Marquette, Wisconsin-Madison, and Tübingen. He held posts at Duquesne University (1960–1966) and served as professor at Temple University from 1966 to 2022.

Leonard van der Kuijp specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned doctorates at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, later serving at the University of Washington (circa 1987–1995) and Harvard University (appointed 1995).

Leopold Pospisil studied at Charles University, Willamette, University of Oregon, and Yale. He served as a professor at Yale University from 1956 and curator at the Peabody Museum of Natural History from circa 1956 to 1993.

Leopold von Schroeder worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at Tartu, Leipzig, Jena, and Tübingen. He held academic posts at the University of Tartu (1882–1890s), Innsbruck (1896), and Vienna (appointed 1899).

Leslie S. Kawamura worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Günther (circa 1971–1975) and served on the faculty at the University of Calgary from circa 1976 to 2010.

Levi McLaughlin works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his dissertation at Princeton under Jacqueline I. Stone, later becoming associate professor at North Carolina State University in 2012.

Lewis Doney specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed an MA under Ulrich Pagel and earned his PhD at SOAS University of London, later holding posts at the University of Munich (attested 2018) and University of Bonn (attested 2021).

Lewis Hodous worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies after studying at Case Western, Hartford International University, and Halle-Wittenberg. He served as president of Foochow Union Theological School (1902–1917) and professor at Hartford International University (1917–1945).

Lewis Lancaster worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology, completing his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as professor at the University of California, Berkeley (circa 1967–2002) and president of University of the West (1992).

id: P:Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk
summary: Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Lhagpa Phuntshogs is a Tibetologist who served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991), secretary-general of the Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000), and director general of the China Tibetology Research Center (appointed 2000).
Liang Cai works in Sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Daniel Boucher and held a post as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas, attested in 2014.

Libbie Mills works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson by 2011 and taught Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto, attested in 2020.
Lili Zheng works in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi, attested in 2011.
Lilian Silburn worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied under Paul Masson-Oursel and Swami Lakshman Joo, and held a post at the CNRS from circa 1950 to 1978.
Lin He was a philosopher who studied at Tsinghua University (National Tsing Hua University) from circa 1919 to 1926 and later held a faculty post there from circa 1931 to 1937.
